blindSummary:
Trans visitors face serious risk here — this country was once its region's relative haven, now regressing. In 2023-2024 it adopted two discriminatory laws targeting the LGBTI community and restricting LGBTI organisations, accompanied by homophobic and transphobic rhetoric from legislators; a trans-rights monitoring network lists it (2021) among the countries that removed legal gender recognition entirely (a 2020 civil-registry law blocks birth-certificate changes). Same-sex conduct is legal (1998), but police abuse and extortion of LGBT people are documented, and the community's main organisation operates under pressure.

For a visitor: no expression statute, but the legal-gender-recognition removal plus a police extortion culture and an active anti-LGBT political campaign make outing risky.
blindOutOfScope: The legal-gender-recognition removal is resident-facing; the NGO-restriction laws signal the enforcement climate.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: two discriminatory laws (2023-2024) target the LGBTI community and restrict organisations, amid homophobic political rhetoric; since 2021 trans people cannot obtain legal recognition (amendments to the civil-registry law); in 2024 a provision of the health law was amended to bar gender-transition-related medical examination or treatment until age 25 (previously 18); a regional trans-health network's data show high stigma from law enforcement and healthcare workers, with police abuse of power.

Trans-rights monitoring network index launch (May 2024): documents polarisation in trans rights across the wider region - progress in some countries (the top-ranked states in the index) and alarming regressions elsewhere, notably a large regional state's July 2023 ban on medical and legal transition; two new indicators added for 2024.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity decriminalised 1998 (equal age of consent 16); a 2016 constitutional amendment bans same-sex marriage; the provision allowing some trans people to change markers was removed in 2020; in early 2026 a legislator proposed a bill defining sex as immutable, explicitly banning legal gender recognition and prohibiting any interventions on minors; this follows the 2023-2024 advocacy-restriction laws.

Regional trans-health network study (2024) on trans people's access to medical services including HIV prevention and hormone therapy across the wider region (with country coordinators in nine regional states) - includes information for trans migrants.

International human-rights organisation's world report 2020, chapter on this country: includes a sexual-orientation and gender-identity section - documents the worsening environment for LGBT people, including a 'gay propaganda' bill and violence against women.

Externally funded international radio service (June 2017): the capital's only LGBT club closed amid a worsening atmosphere - its founder said people don't understand what a gay club is and assume it is pornographic, but that visitors would see it is just a normal club.

Foreign broadsheet feature (Oct 2017) on why the capital's only gay club closed: the city had long been a liberal beacon within its region until the 'LGBT propaganda' ban; with attacks and rapes on the rise, community members warn that all of them will be victims at some point, and the community is scared.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2020 law blocking birth-certificate changes (legal-gender-recognition removal) is resident-facing; the NGO-restriction laws affect resident organisations.
